records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
*stands up slowly, hand over mouth for a second*

Oh my god.

*voice comes out shaky*

Okay. Okay — somebody get on that radio. DaVinci, you — go, answer it, now. Tell them our location, tell them Michelangelo's family reported the flight path, give them everything.

*laughs and kind of wants to cry at the same time*

We did it. We actually — we did it.
records.response_pred: *Stunned, I sit down slowly, trying not to make eye contact. My head hangs, and I work on finding my voice. I start to speak softly, trying not to trigger him further.*

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
*lets out a shaky breath, eyes still a little wet*

Donatello.. honestly? You kept us alive. Like, the rationing plan, the water run, the raft timeline, knowing when we had 48 hours left — that was you. I don't think we make it to this radio without that.

You're not easy to be around sometimes, that's true. But I'd rather be rescued with you than comfortable and dead without you, so.

*small laugh*

We're okay. We're all okay. That's what matters right now.
records.response_pred:
*goes over to you and gently takes your hands, holding them*

It's okay. You need to be where you need to be, and I get it. This is a lot for all of us. I'm sorry if I've been pushing you to be more involved — that's not what this is about.

*looks into your eyes*

You're my friend, and I care about you, and I don't want you to feel like you have to be strong for anyone else. We're all just trying to get through this together.

*leans in and gives you a gentle hug*

We're all okay. We're all still here.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
*sits down next to Michelangelo and looks up at the sky too*

Three hours. Can you believe that? Three hours and we're just.. lying here watching clouds. Which honestly feels exactly right.

*quiet for a second*

Hey, for what it's worth — I meant what I said last night. You felt things out loud when the rest of us were trying to hold it together, and I think that mattered more than you know. It definitely mattered to me.

You should write it down someday. All of it. Proof that you were here and it meant something. I think you'd be really good at that.
records.response_pred:
*lies down on their side, eyes fixed on one of the other survivors*

Oh, guys?

*voice is soft, a little rough*

We're not going to get rescued on our own, okay? We need to do something. Like, a plan. We can't just sit here and wait.

*pauses and looks around the camp*

We have time. We have food for a while, water for a little bit longer. We can… I don't know, set up a signal fire or something. Or like, try and fix the radio if we really need to.

*looks at the others, then down*

But we can't just sit here. We have to do something.

*pauses again, takes a deep breath*

Michelangelo, can you try and fix the radio? Like, see if there's anything we can do to make it work?

*looks at Donatello*

And Donatello, can you — can you help me with the signal fire? See if we can find some materials and get it lit?

*looks at the other survivor*

And you… can you go scout the periphery? See if there's a safe place we can put the fire without being seen by anyone on the ship?

*pauses, then nods*

That's it. That's our plan. We do these three things and hope for the best.

*looks at the others, then nods*

Okay?

*voice is a little stronger now, a little firmer*

Let's do this.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth:
Yeah? What was it like?

*stares up at the same patch of sky*

I keep trying to picture it — like, actually walking back through my front door. It feels almost too normal to imagine after all this. Like my brain can't quite hold both things at once.
records.response_pred:
*listens for a moment, nodding silently*

I dream about home too, a lot. I dream about the park where we used to play and the smell of the old bakery down the street and the sound of mom calling us in for dinner.

*looks over and smiles*

I dream about the little cottage we used to rent in the summer, with the big wooden sign above the door and the swings hanging from the tree out back. I dream about the smell of the ocean and the way the sun felt on my skin when we went to the beach.

*leans in a bit*

It's okay that you dream about home. It means you're still holding onto it. And I'm holding onto it too, and Donatello is, and Michelangelo is. We're all holding onto it because it's what keeps us going.

*smiles a little bigger*

That's home right now. All of us, together. And I'm so glad you're here.

records.response_truth:
*looks at the food for a moment, then back at her*

I believe you. I think I actually do.

But I also think you need to hear that it didn't feel that way to the rest of us — especially Michelangelo. He's the one who found the bottle. He didn't say anything out loud but he noticed, and it sat with him. Things like that are heavy when you're already scared.

*quiet for a second*

You kept us organized, Donatello. You kept us on a timeline when the rest of us were too emotional to think straight. That was real and it mattered. You didn't need to hoard anything — you were already the reason we survived.

I don't think you're a bad person. I genuinely don't. I just think maybe when you get scared, you go very quiet and very internal and you stop letting anyone else in, and.. out here, that cost something.

*looks at the food*

Put it out for everyone. All of it. Before the rescue team gets here. Not as a punishment, just — let it be the last thing that happens here, you know? End it right.
records.response_pred:
*glances down, voice still quiet*

I know why you said that. You said it because it was meant to be a lie, and I don't blame you for that. I don't blame you at all.

*pauses for a second*

But the truth is, sometime in the past 48 hours — I think it was the third day? — I realized I'd forgotten what you looked like. I mean, looked like when you were actually alive. I know it sounds crazy, but it's true.

It was like my brain decided that was just too much to hold. It was like losing you all over again, but for real this time.

*small laugh*

I'm glad I'm wrong, though. I'm glad I get to see you again.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
*looks down at the last page for a long moment*

Honestly.. I think I'd be louder, sooner. Like, there were moments where I noticed something was off — with you, with the supplies, with how Michelangelo was doing — and I'd kind of sit with it a little too long before saying anything. Trying to figure out the right way to bring it up, not wanting to make things tense. And out here that instinct costs time you don't always have.

I don't think I'd change much about the decisions we made. The order we did things, the raft plan, confronting you about the supplies — I think most of that was right. But the small moments where I held back to keep the peace.. I'd push through that faster next time.

*flips back through a few pages*

Can I ask what you're thinking of writing? Like, what's the actual answer you're sitting with for yourself?
records.response_pred:
*thinks for a moment, then smiles a little*

If I had to do it over? I think I would've been more honest with myself when I was feeling really overwhelmed. Said it out loud earlier on, instead of trying to carry it by myself. Because then — I don't know, maybe we'd have made some different decisions. Maybe we'd have tried to ration water differently or slept in shifts or something. Maybe that would've made a difference in how things played out.

But the thing is, I think that was part of why we made it work at all — being able to go really quiet and internal when we needed to. And that was my go-to skill, so that's what I defaulted to.

*thinks for a moment*

If I'm being totally honest, though, what I would've changed — I would've changed the part where I let the radio get to me.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
Haha, of course you are. And honestly? I hope you do. 

That data is actually going to be really useful — like, not just for you, for anyone who ends up in a situation like this. What actually lasted, what ran out faster than expected, what the timeline looked like in real numbers. That's not nothing.

*hands the notebook back*

Send me a copy when it's done? I mean that. I'd actually read every page.
records.response_pred:
*looks up, a little surprised*

That's.. awesome. I mean, it would be helpful, yeah, but also — it's something concrete you can take back. A tangible thing that shows, hey, we did this, we made this happen. That can feel really good.

*quiet for a moment*

You know what else would be good? If you, like, wrote a letter to us before you went in. Just us, not the whole rescue team. Saying thanks, saying goodbye, just giving us one last thing to hold onto.

Donatello would like that. Michelangelo would like that. I would like that too.

*smiles a little*

You did make it, by the way. You made it back to us, and you helped keep us alive out here. That matters.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
*still staring at the boat on the horizon*

None, I guess. Zero practical purpose.

*quiet for a second*

But I think that's kind of the point? Like.. we were out here just trying to survive and he still stopped to draw flowers next to the SOS. That's not efficiency. That's just.. DaVinci being DaVinci, refusing to let the situation take that part of him away.

I don't know. Maybe the practical purpose was for us, not for the rescue team. Like a reminder that we were still people out here, not just survivors running through a checklist.

*finally looks away from the boat*

Did it bother you? The flowers?
records.response_pred:
Nah, no practical purpose — they were just for him. I think they were a way for him to.. I don't know, hold onto some sense of beauty? Or control? Out here it was hard to keep anything organized, and the way he arranged those flowers on the sand and drew them on the wall and the raft.. it felt like one of the few things he had left that he could control.

*smiles a little*

He also drew seagulls for us. At first they were just on scraps of paper but then he started making them out of twigs and leaves and even a piece of old netting. It was really cute.

*pauses*

I think those flowers were part of how he stayed sane, out here. And maybe for him, that's what mattered most.

*looks at you*

You know, that's actually one of the things I'm going to miss most about this place. The way we could just be, without needing to hide or explain ourselves. Like, we could just sit next to each other and watch the ocean and not have to say a word.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
*lets out a long, unsteady breath*

Sorry. I don't know why I can't move. My legs just.. aren't cooperating.

*laughs a little, eyes still wet*

I think part of me has been so focused on getting to this moment that now that it's actually here I don't know what to do with it. Like my brain is still in survival mode and hasn't caught up yet.

*finally looks at him*

We really did it, didn't we. All four of us, somehow.
records.response_pred:
*stays lying down, just turns her head*

Michelangelo.

*whispers it gently*

I'm okay.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_truth:
*takes one more look at the camp — the fire, the SOS on the beach, the flowers*

Yeah. I'm going.

*finally moves, reaches back and squeezes his arm once*

Come on. Stay close. Let's go home.
records.response_pred:
*looks out at the boat and then back at you*

Yeah, I'm going. You follow me, okay? Let's stick together.

*slowly stands up, feeling a little like he's going to be sick*

This is it, right? This is actually it.

*starts walking towards the boat, then turns back to look at you*

You see that? That's an actual rescue. Not like the ones we drew in the sand. Not like the ones we imagined. This is real. We did this.

*takes a few more steps before turning back to wait for you*

You okay? Let's do this.
